First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5\pi }{12})-{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{5\pi }{12}) & =cos\,(2\cdot \frac{5\pi }{12}) \\  & =cos\,(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
